map.血糖负荷 GL = GI × 可消化碳水(g) ÷ 100，其中 GI 为血糖生: Glycemic load GL = GI × digestible carbohydrate(g) ÷ 100, where GI is the glycemic index (glucose 100 as the baseline); GL of 20 or more is a high load, 11 to 19 a medium load, and 10 or less a low load; total daily GL is recommended to stay under 80, and people managing blood sugar should pick foods with a low GI and a GL within 10.

map.GL = GI × 可用碳水(g) / 100。白米饭 GI 83、一份碳水 5: GL = GI × available carbohydrate(g) / 100. Plain white rice has GI 83 and a 50 g carbohydrate portion → GL = 83×50/100 = 41.5 (high load); an apple has GI 36 and 15 g carbohydrate → GL = 5.4 (low load).
map.GL≤10 低负荷、11–20 中负荷、>20 高负荷；西瓜 GI 72 但一份: GL≤10 is a low load, 11-20 a medium load and >20 a high load; watermelon has GI 72 but about 11 g carbohydrate per portion → GL≈7.9, a low load instead, so quantity matters too.
map.GI 和 GL 差在哪？: What is the difference between GI and GL?
map.GI 只看升糖速度、不含量；GL 同时乘实际碳水，更贴近真实血糖负担，选食更实用: GI only looks at how fast blood sugar rises and ignores quantity, while GL multiplies in the actual carbohydrate and therefore reflects the real blood sugar burden, which makes it more practical for food choice.
map.低 GI 就能多吃吗？: Does a low GI mean I can eat more?
map.不能，低 GI 但吃大量碳水 GL 仍高；控糖看 GL 并控总碳水与份量。: No. A low GI with a large amount of carbohydrate still gives a high GL; control GL and also keep total carbohydrate and portion size in check.
